items.title: Peel police sign 'first-of-its-kind' pact with Human Rights Commission to implement dozens of anti-racism recommendations
items.summary: The agreement will see a new independent oversight process to help drive “meaningful, measurable change” against systemic racism. Peel Regional Police Chief Nishan Duraiappah lauded the agreement as a concrete step in building trust with residents. The force started consultations to help address systemic racism back in 2020. A new independent body will be tasked with guiding the implementation of more than 65 recommendations to address systemic racism within Peel police, after a “first-of-its-kind” agreement was struck between the service, its board and the Ontario Human Rights Commission (OHRC). The binding arbitration accord, announced Tuesday, aims to enact a wide range of recommendations to eliminate racial discrimination, such as the further prohibition of police street checks and carding the use of de-escalation techniques, and emphasizing organizational change through hiring and training. ” “Policing must be fair, equitable, and free from systemic bias. This first-of-its-kind agreement demonstrates our leadership in driving meaningful, measurable change through transparent, independent oversight,” he said in a statement. The three organizations say the recommendations were made by the OHRC through the Human Rights Project, which began in February 2020.

items.title: Trapeze Duo Behind Canada's First Quadruple Somersault Set to Perform in Mississauga This Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, the Royal Canadian Circus is bringing a newly set Canadian first with it when it arrives in Mississauga this month, days after a milestone performance in Scarborough. Circus officials said trapeze duo The Flying Poema completed Canada's first-ever quadruple somersault during the closing weekend of a 10-day run at Scarborough Town Centre. INsauga reports officials described the move as an extremely rare feat that only a handful of performers worldwide have ever landed, and said The Flying Poema plans to attempt it again at future stops on the tour. The circus, currently marking its 52nd anniversary Canadian tour, will set up in the parking lot of Dixie Outlet Mall in Mississauga's east end from August 21 to 30, following a similar 10-day stay at the same mall in August 2025. INsauga notes the Mississauga stop is part of an all-new 2026 production that has already toured through Hamilton, Brampton, Newmarket, Markham and Vaughan, with Burlington next up on the schedule from September 3 to 7.

items.title: Studio.89 Will Shut Its Eglinton Avenue Storefront But Keep Its Community Programs Running
items.summary: According to INsauga, Studio.89, a non-profit fair trade and vegan cafe that has also served as a community hub in Mississauga, announced on Instagram that it will close its brick-and-mortar location on September 14. INsauga reports the cafe has operated at 2520 Eglinton Avenue West, offering espresso drinks, coffee, smoothies, sandwiches and treats as a social enterprise that funnels sales toward its social, cultural and environmental mission. This isn't the first time the organization has faced a financial crunch, INsauga notes, pointing to a 2018 fundraising push that brought in a $50,000 donation to help keep the cafe's doors open. Even after the physical space closes, Studio.89 says it plans to keep running its community programming at venues across Mississauga, according to INsauga. Those programs include initiatives focused on art as a tool for social change, climate action, youth leadership, connections between youth and seniors, and job skills training.

items.title: Chef Matty Matheson's Maker Pizza Chain Set to Open Its Fifth Location in Mississauga
items.summary: According to WhatNow, Maker Pizza, the pizza chain founded by celebrity chef Matty Matheson and business partner Shlomo Buchler, is set to open a new location at 181 City Centre Drive in Mississauga in late August. WhatNow reports the Mississauga shop will mark the brand's fifth location since it launched in 2015 with an original spot on Cameron Street. The new store joins existing Maker Pizza locations on Cameron Street, Bayview Avenue and Carlaw Avenue in Toronto, along with a Bathurst Street shop in Thornhill. According to the report, the menu sells pizza by the slice or whole pie, with specialty options including Siena Margherita, Napoli Dynamite, Dr. Pepperoni and Tropic Thunder. WhatNow notes the shop also offers a range of dips, such as creamy garlic, dill ranch and spicy creamy garlic, along with wings and garlic fingers.

items.title: Independent Verifier Will Check Whether Peel Police Follows Through on Anti-Racism Recommendations
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police will now face independent oversight to verify whether it is actually carrying out recommendations meant to eliminate racial profiling and systemic discrimination within the force. INsauga reports the new agreement between Peel Regional Police, the Peel Police Services Board and the Ontario Human Rights Commission sets up a process to check on implementation and resolve disputes between the three parties, including through binding arbitration if needed. The recommendations trace back to a Human Rights Project the three organizations launched in 2020, which involved consultations with Black, Indigenous and other racialized communities and led to an initial set of recommendations released in 2023. According to INsauga, those recommendations are built on seven principles developed by the OHRC, covering areas such as acknowledging systemic racism, community engagement, policy changes, accountability, organizational change and data collection. Under the new agreement, the three organizations will jointly select an independent verifier, with support from the community-based Anti-Racism Advisory Committee, to assess the department's progress, INsauga notes.

items.title: Crews Finish Twin Tunnels Linking Crosstown LRT Extension Toward Mississauga and Pearson Airport
items.summary: According to INsauga, Metrolinx says crews have finished tunnelling on twin 500-metre tunnels running between Jane Street and Mount Dennis Station in Toronto, connecting the Eglinton Crosstown West Extension to the existing Line 5 Eglinton line. INsauga reports the underground work began in February and took roughly six months to complete, marking what project leaders called a critical milestone for the transit expansion. The extension will carry Line 5 Eglinton farther west to bring rapid transit service to Etobicoke and Mississauga, and is expected to eventually reach north from the Mississauga-Toronto border toward Toronto Pearson Airport. INsauga notes the provincial government has said the completed extension will help reduce gridlock and connect nearly 70,000 commuters to jobs across the Greater Toronto Area. Ontario Premier Doug Ford said earlier this summer that the government is making what he called historic investments in the largest public transit expansion in North America to support commuters and fight gridlock.

items.title: York Police Say Mississauga Man's Alleged Online Luring Scheme Spanned Two Separate Investigations
items.summary: According to a York Regional Police release, a 52-year-old Mississauga man has been charged in connection with a child luring investigation involving youths under 16. Police say the investigation began last September after they identified a man allegedly using an online platform to arrange meetings with youths he believed were under 16 for the purpose of committing sexual offences. According to police, the Ontario Provincial Police notified York investigators in May 2026 that they were looking into similar allegations involving the same suspect and motive, and the man was charged in June 2026 in connection with both investigations. Investigators have released a photograph of the accused because they believe there may be additional victims who haven't yet come forward. Police are asking anyone with information to contact York Regional Police at 1-866-876-5423, extension 7078.

items.title: New First Aid and Aquatic Leadership Courses Headline Mississauga's Fall Recreation Lineup
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, city residents can now register for Mississauga's fall recreation programs through Active Mississauga, with in-person registration also available at community centres during service desk hours. The lineup includes Swim for Life lessons, which build swimming and water-safety skills through step-by-step instruction for different ages and skill levels, along with aquatic leadership courses meant to give youth and young adults a pathway toward careers such as lifeguarding and swim instruction. Mississauga.com reports a new Intermediate First Aid course, formerly known as Standard First Aid, is being offered this fall and covers how to respond to emergencies including allergic reactions, strokes, burns, fractures, seizures, diabetic emergencies and environmental injuries. That course also includes CPR-C and AED certification, which the city notes is a prerequisite for the more advanced Bronze Cross certification. The city is also offering a range of preschool programs guided by the HIGH FIVE quality standard, according to Mississauga.com.

items.title: Next Hydrogen Completes Engineering Design for 10 MW Fueling Station in Expanding British Columbia Market

(“Next Hydrogen” or the “Company”) (TSXV:NXH) is pleased to announce that it has completed a Basic Design Engineering Package (BDEP) for a planned 10 MW fueling station in British Columbia, Canada, with a confidential customer (the “BC Project”). MISSISSAUGA, Ontario, Aug. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — Next Hydrogen Solutions Inc. (“Next Hydrogen” or the “Company”) (TSXV:NXH) is pleased to announce that it has completed a Basic Design Engineering Package (BDEP) for a planned 10 MW fueling station in British Columbia, Canada, with a confidential customer (the “BC Project”). The planned project would support BC’s decarbonization plans for the critically important transportation sector. British Columbia continues to invest heavily in hydrogen technology, leveraging local hydroelectricity capacity and a strong clean-tech sector. CleanBC’s Roadmap to 2030 remains the overarching strategy for decarbonization, with transportation as the largest emissions sector. Hydrogen is increasingly positioned for medium- and heavy-duty vehicles, where batteries face range and charging-time constraints. Hydrogen-fueled trucks are now being tested in BC’s Lower Mainland where freight corridors and Hydrogen Hubs are advancing within the Province1. The BC Project design is based upon Next Hydrogen’s Made-in-Canada, commercially deployed containerized electrolysers. A Financial Investment Decision (FID) for the BDEP Project is anticipated by the end of 2026. The BDEP enables full definition and costing of the BC Project as a key input to the FID process.

Appointment of President and Chief Executive Officer The Board of Directors is pleased to announce the appointment of Jocelyne Moyer as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Next Hydrogen and its subsidiaries and a director of the Company effective September 1, 2026. As previously announced, Raveel Afzaal, will transition from the CEO role and leave the board as of August 31, 2026. She also worked from 2016 to 2022 at Bain & Company advising senior executive teams of industry leading companies on critical strategic issues. Ms. Moyer joined Heliolytics in 2022 as Director of Strategy and Operations and became General Manager in 2023, shortly before its acquisition by Zeitview.

items.title: 141 New Units Proposed for Three Modular Towers on Ninth Line in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the City of Mississauga is reviewing a proposal from Mattamy Homes for three modular six-storey apartment buildings at 6344 Ninth Line, just south of Doug Leavens Boulevard. Mississauga.com reports the three towers would together add 141 units to the site. The application asks the city to change the zoning bylaw currently in place so the development can go ahead. According to the report, the proposal also includes additional landscape and public realm enhancements planned around the perimeter of the property. Mississauga.com notes a public meeting on the application has been scheduled for September 21, giving residents a chance to weigh in before the city makes a decision.

items.title: City Reminds Homeowners That Backyard Projects May Require a Tree Permit First
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, residents planning a backyard project such as installing a pool, building a deck or removing a tree should first check whether the work requires a tree permit. The city says trees on both private and public property are protected under Mississauga's tree protection by-laws, which were updated in 2022 to ensure trees across the city are managed responsibly. Checking before cutting can help residents avoid fines, delays and unexpected costs, according to the city, while also protecting Mississauga's broader urban forest. City officials note that healthy trees do more than improve the look of a neighbourhood, since they also provide shade, improve air quality, absorb rainwater and help reduce the effects of extreme heat. As Mississauga experiences hotter summers and more extreme weather, the city says protecting its tree canopy helps keep neighbourhoods cooler, healthier and more resilient.
